conceptZh: 陽：太陽的光，左邊是土丘（阜），右邊是太陽升起的樣子。
object: a boxy mismatched-parts toy robot with one very long arm, a big glossy toy sun with rosy cheeks
morph: two teams tug a rope: robot pulls the sun's side, the sun pulls the hill side, and the two halves of 陽 spring together
creativeAngle: 玩具機器人與玩具太陽拔河，一拉一扯讓左右兩半彈在一起；長短手機器人用長手臂把太陽拉上來。
promptEn: An 8-second bright, clean 2D/3D toy-animation clip. Teaching subject: the single Traditional Chinese glyph 陽 (sun / sunshine), correctly formed, in a saturated solid color against a much lighter background, ending centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height with margins. Lead cast: a boxy mismatched-parts toy robot with one very long arm, a big glossy toy sun with rosy cheeks. Soft sky-blue backdrop with a small sandy-yellow hill mound at the bottom; the glyph is built in deep sunset-orange. Timed beats. 0.0-1.5s: the boxy toy robot (mismatched copper and teal parts, long left arm) marches in dragging a thick rope that runs off the right edge. As it plants its feet, the voice says the first 陽 and a faint orange outline of the left half (the hill radical) appears at center, bobbing. 1.5-3.0s: the rope tightens and a rosy-cheeked toy sun slides up from the right edge, gripping the other end with both rays. They tug-of-war; the robot's long arm stretches comically while the sun squeaks backwards. The voice says the second 陽 as the two orange halves of the glyph stretch apart like taffy. 3.0-4.5s: the rope snaps slack, robot and sun both shoot back, and the two halves spring together with a boing into the finished solid orange 陽 at about 70% of frame height. The robot tumbles onto its back with its legs spinning. 4.5-5.0s: the voice says 太陽 (ㄊㄞˋ ㄧㄤˊ) as the real toy sun hops up beside the glyph and beams warm rays across the robot, who flips upright and salutes with the long arm. Final hold: 5.0-8.0s: the glyph is perfectly still. The sun gently sways and the robot waves its mismatched arms off to the side, never touching the strokes. The glyph holds fully still and clearly readable for the last 3 seconds. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen narrator speaks slowly and distinctly in clear Taiwanese Mandarin (Taiwan standard readings, no erhua), reading exactly these syllables with clear tones: 陽、陽、太陽 (ㄧㄤˊ、ㄧㄤˊ、ㄊㄞˋ ㄧㄤˊ). Say the character twice with a short pause, then the word once, and stop; no other speech, subtitles or loud music. The vocabulary word is audio only. The glyph 陽 is the only text on screen: no subtitles, captions, labels, watermark, logos, clutter, flashing or strobing effects, and no real people or realistic human figures; all characters are stylized toys or cartoon animals.
